svg.title: Dye versus pigment
svg.desc: Schematic comparing a dye dissolved and fixed inside a fibre with pigment particles held in a binder on a surface
svg.text: Dyes dissolve and bond to the fibre; pigments are insoluble particles held on the surface by a binder
fibre: dye held INSIDE by ionic / H-bond / van der Waals / covalent forces
vehicle / binder with insoluble particles (≈ 0.1–1 µm)
particles stay ON the surface in a binder film
Dye: soluble / finely dispersed in the medium; has affinity (substantivity) for the fibre; transparent; e.g. methyl orange, indigo, alizarin.
Pigment: insoluble in water and solvents; no affinity, needs binder; opaque or translucent; e.g. TiO₂ (white), phthalocyanine blue, carbon black, Fe₂O₃.
Lake pigment: a dye precipitated on an inorganic base (e.g. alizarin on Al(OH)₃) – shares properties of both.
